hypotheses.statement: solang accepts explicit narrowing conversions from signed to unsigned integer types of different widths (e.g. int16 -> uint8) that solc >=0.8 rejects with 'Explicit type conversion not allowed'. This creates compile-time asymmetry for any seed using direct signed->unsigned narrowing casts; such specs only exercise solang and mask runtime divergences.

evidence.note: COMPILE_ASYMMETRY: solc rejected uint8(x) where x is int16; solang compiled fine. Runtime steps never executed on EVM side.

hypotheses.next_probe: Minimal compile-only probe: contract with function f(int16 x) returns (uint8) { return uint8(x); } compiled by both toolchains. Expect solc reject / solang accept. Also try int8 -> uint16 and int32 -> uint128 to map the scope of the asymmetry.

hypotheses.statement: solang's runtime semantics for the two-step legal cast chain (int16 -> int8 -> uint8 -> uint64 -> int64, i.e. truncate then zero-extend) match solc's: int16(-1) yields 255, not -1. If solang instead sign-extends through the chain (yields -1) that is a codegen bug.

evidence.note: Cast semantics untested: solc compile failure blocked all runtime comparison.

hypotheses.next_probe: Rewrite doCast as int64(uint64(uint8(int8(x)))) — legal in both compilers — call with -1, query lastCast; expect 255 on both.

hypotheses.statement: solang agrees with solc on signed division/modulo truncation toward zero (-7/2==-3, -7%2==-1), arithmetic shift right on signed ints (-8>>1==-4), and the int8 overflow edge case -128 / -1 (solc >=0.8 reverts on overflow). No evidence yet because the probe died at compile time.

evidence.note: Div/mod/shift behavior never observed due to compile asymmetry; hypothesis carries zero runtime evidence.

hypotheses.next_probe: Same spec minus the doCast function (drop lastCast and its step): run doDivMod(-7,2), doShift(-8), doDivMod(-128,-1), then query lastDiv/lastMod/lastShift. Compare revert behavior and stored values.
